title: Three stratified layers of substrate grain, metric moduli, and empirical unit bridges
html:
Seven notions of step size, clock period, distance, volume, and physical length enter across the paper. Grouping them by what algebraic structure each requires resolves every apparent symbol collision into three stratified layers separated by two base-ring boundaries: the rational algebra of an arbitrary field k with q \in k^\times \setminus \{1\} (Tier 1), order and supremum bounds over an ordered or archimedean field \mathbb{R} (Tier 2), and empirical conversion functors into SI units (Tier 3).

Layer Quantity Defining expression Base-ring tier Role in model

I Full-circuit tick & unit circuit t_P(q) = \hbar_q^{-1}, \;\hbar_q t_P(q) = 1 Tier 1: field k, q \in k^\times \setminus \{1\} Normalised Reeb period; internal G_{\mathrm{Planck}} = 1
I Thomae--Jackson proper-time lattice \tau_j = \tau_0 q^{2j}, \;\sum_{j < N} q^{-j} < t_P(q) Tier 1 sum; Tier 2 ceiling (q > 1) Ultraviolet geometric sum bounded by t_P(q); proportional to Borel/Reeb clocks under step atomicity
IIa Connes--Kantorovich--Rubinstein metric d_L(\varphi,\psi) = \sup_{L(a)\le 1} \lvert\varphi(a)-\psi(a)\rvert Tier 2: ordered field \mathbb{R} State-space transport metric on faithful quotient TL_n(q) = H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}
IIb Hyperbolic cusp 3-volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) Tier 2: archimedean \mathbb{R} Dimensionless mass-carrier modulus (\mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Hopf}) = 0; distinct from spatial radius)

IIIb SI gravitational bridge \ell_{\mathrm{Planck}}^{\mathrm{SI}} = \sqrt{\hbar G_{\mathrm{Newton}}/c^3} Tier 3: empirical SI (G_{\mathrm{Newton}} chart) External Newton--Planck length, separated from \lambda_{C,e} by 2.4 \times 10^{22}

Layer I: Dimensionless \mathbb{Q}(q) grain and atomic clock

Every rational-function scale in the algebraic substrate derives from the single primitive \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} = (q-1)/q, defined over any field k at q \in k^\times \setminus \{1\}. That one element supplies the per-step Reeb share of D_\nabla (Reeb coefficient identity), the brane-fluid viscous cutoff scale 2\nu_q = \hbar_q opposing compression at short wavelengths, the reciprocal full-circuit tick t_P(q) = \hbar_q^{-1} = q/(q-1) whose product with the share is the unit-normalised Reeb circuit \hbar_q\, t_P(q) = 1 (discrete Planck step; share versus total), and the internal gravitational identity G_{\mathrm{Planck}} = G(q)(\hbar_q / c_q)^2 = 1 (gravitational constant). Retiring the auxiliary glyphs \ell_P^{\mathrm{step}} and \ell_q in favour of \hbar_q keeps one symbol for one rational function across fluid dynamics and information theory.

On the Thomae--Jackson proper-time lattice \tau_j = \tau_0 q^{2j}, the ultraviolet partial sum satisfies the algebraic identity

  \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \bigl(q^{-1}\bigr)^j \;=\; \frac{1 - (q^{-1})^N}{1 - q^{-1}} \;=\; \bigl(1 - (q^{-1})^N\bigr)\, t_P(q)

over any field k with q \in k^\times \setminus \{1\}. Imposing a linear order with q > 1 (Tier 2) yields (q^{-1})^N > 0 and 1 - q^{-1} > 0, bounding every finite ultraviolet sum strictly below the full-circuit tick t_P(q) = \hbar_q^{-1}. Under the atomic-step monoid premise --- that every substrate computation segment is an iterate of one indivisible step --- any two additive clocks on the step monoid differ by a single nonzero scalar, uniting Borel jet time, Thomae--Jackson proper time, and Reeb circuit counts up to scale.

Layer II: Dimensionless state and 3-manifold moduli

Passing to an ordered archimedean ground field introduces two dimensionless geometric invariants that act on different spaces and carry distinct meanings. First, Leonid V. Kantorovich [kantorovich1942], Gennady Sh. Rubinstein [rubinstein1957], Alain Connes [connes1989], and Marc A. Rieffel [rieffel1999, rieffel2004] define a state-space transport distance d_L(\varphi,\psi) from a Lipschitz seminorm L [dandrea-martinetti2010]. Because non-scalar kernel elements send that supremum to infinity (degeneracy obstruction), d_L lives on the faithful Temperley--Lieb quotient TL_n(q) = H_n(q)/\mathrm{rad}, where D_\nabla weights horizontal gradient transport by q^{-1} and Reeb contact transport by \hbar_q (Reeb-step-count qualification). Second, the hyperbolic cusp 3-volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) is a topological invariant of the knot complement entering the mass operator: the non-hyperbolic Hopf link has \mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Hopf}) = 0, and equal cusp volumes on the mirror nuclei {}^3\mathrm{H} and {}^3\mathrm{He} alongside distinct charge radii rule out treating \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)^{1/3} as a Euclidean spatial radius.

Layer III: Dimensionful unit-bridge functors

Physical units enter at the boundary where dimensionless ratios meet empirical standards. The first calibration input (m_e) defines the electroweak Compton functor \lambda_{C,e} = \hbar / (m_e c), which converts dimensionless quantities into laboratory lengths and times including the Compton period t_C, the pion Yukawa scale r_\pi, and the deformed de Broglie wavelength \lambda_q = q\,\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}. A separate empirical chart introduces Newton's constant G_{\mathrm{Newton}} to form the SI Planck length \ell_{\mathrm{Planck}}^{\mathrm{SI}} = \sqrt{\hbar G_{\mathrm{Newton}}/c^3}, separated from \lambda_{C,e} by the dimensionless electroweak--Planck ratio outside the three-mass calibration basis.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0, the D_\nabla Lipschitz split places q_0^{-1} \approx 90.09\,\% weight on horizontal gradient transport and \hbar_{q_0} \approx 9.91\,\% on Reeb transport, with t_P(q_0) \approx 10.09, while in SI units the Compton--Planck ratio \lambda_{C,e} / \ell_{\mathrm{Planck}}^{\mathrm{SI}} is \approx 2.4 \times 10^{22}.
